main_text.l: ad humum defluat. Despumatum quoque minus excrementosum esse, frigido ventriculo optimum nutrimentum, magisque nutrire idem afferit lib. eodem. Crudum enim aluum inflare tuffimq; lacessere deprehensum est. Coquendum est autem supra pru-nas aut arida ligna sine fumo, ac probè despumandum. Unde tutior etiam eius in medicinis est usus, medicique ad occurrendum corruptionibus, putredinemq; compescen-dam in mellis usu sunt audaciores.

Ad extremum non ignorandum, esse adhuc alia duo mellis genera, unum Saccharum vocatum Indi, quod India fert & Arabia, mel videlicet in arundinib. concretum gummi aut salis modo candidum ac fri-abile, unde Megasthenes graecus Indiam mel, sine apum opificio gignere tradit: alterum ab aeris rore ἀέρομελι [?] id est mel roscidum aut aerium, ab hebr. manna, latin. ros Syriacus dicitur, quoniam interdiu sublato aestiui solis vapore in aera, qui tandem serenae noctis frigore concretus, in Syria & monte Libani, Neapolis, in Oenotria campo, ac Calabria, ante lucano tempore supra saxa, aut laricis arboris, aut thymi, aliarumq; plantarum folia destillat, id collectum inq; mafam globulose effictum ad vsum seponitur. De hoc plura legantur apud Galenum,

page.notes: Marginal notes: "Saccharū" (left, beside the first line of the second paragraph) and "Manna," (left, beside "aut aerium"). The note "j.de" stands in the right margin at the foot. The Greek word ἀέρομελι is uncertain; the printed word is blurred. The printed "mafam" and "vsum" may be printing errors for "massam" and "usum", left as printed. The word "acfri-abile" is printed without a space between "ac" and "fri-", so the space was added. The Greek word and the note "Manna," are doubtful readings.
